one_line: Human-guided manufacturing incident recovery with agent investigation and approved execution.
what_it_does: Models a supplier delay incident, lets an agent inspect risk, inventory, and suppliers, prepare a recovery plan, and execute only after human approval.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools sharing live incident and operational state make multi-step investigation and gated recovery materially more reliable than UI-driving automation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies tools for incident lookup, at-risk orders, inventory, supplier search, planning, approval, execution, and final status.
Frame sheets show a rendered operations app with forms/lists and adjacent WebMCP/tool-inspector UI.
Devpost packaging visibly shows production health, orders at risk, critical material, and a recovery panel.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent incident-to-plan workflow and consistent dashboard/tool surfaces, though no transcript or independently observed live completion is supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and public repository is present.
Frames show multiple rendered application states and tool interaction surfaces.
About text gives a specific 48-hour aluminium shortage scenario and approval boundary.
impact_rationale: Manufacturing and operations teams have a concrete, high-cost incident-recovery problem, and the stated workflow directly addresses coordination and risk.
impact_evidence: Specific supplier delay affecting production and three customer orders.
Visible stated exposure of R423,000 and constrained production health.
Human approval is retained before consequential execution.
creativity_rationale: A focused human-agent incident recovery loop is a strong application of WebMCP, with meaningful approval semantics rather than chat-only advice.
creativity_evidence: Concept combines investigation, option comparison, approval, execution, and verification in one operational dashboard.
The submission explicitly frames the agent as doing work inside the application.
usability_note: Dashboard framing and explicit recovery status appear understandable; operational density may require domain familiarity.
red_flags: No video transcript and visual evidence does not clearly prove the full end-to-end execution path.
Demo appears to use a simulated incident scenario.
standouts: Concrete operational stakes and recovery workflow.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage and credible, well-scoped operational use case with substantial packet evidence.

one_line: Scoped, temporary authority for agent transactions with stale-state protection and receipts.
what_it_does: Turns consequential agent actions into approved, hashed, verified transactions with narrowly scoped commit authority and audit receipts.
leverage_rationale: The product makes the agent surface itself conditional on exact approval and canonical state; this authority model is difficult to reproduce comparably with generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text defines intent, preview, exact-plan approval, scoped authority, commit, verification, and receipt.
Mutation tools appear only after approval and disappear after execution, rejection, revocation, reset, or expiry.
Claims include stale-state, idempotency, invariants, post-condition verification, and audit integrity.
execution_rationale: The protocol design is unusually coherent, but there are no submitted frame sheets, gallery images, or video evidence, so end-to-end execution is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive.
Detailed workflow and reference operations are described in the packet.
No visual or transcript evidence demonstrates the claimed flows.
impact_rationale: Constrained authorization and verification address a central safety problem for agents performing consequential web actions across many domains.
impact_evidence: Explicitly protects billing, deletion, offboarding, ownership transfer, and access revocation operations.
Stale approvals lose commit authority instead of silently applying outdated plans.
Receipts and auditability support accountability.
creativity_rationale: The temporary capability lifecycle and plan-hash-bound authority are a novel, ambitious interaction model for agent/web transactions.
creativity_evidence: Authority is modeled as a first-class transaction-scoped capability rather than permanent tool access.
The packet describes multiple safety invariants and canonical verification as part of the protocol.
usability_note: Exact previews and receipts could build trust, but no UI evidence is supplied to assess usability.
red_flags: No frame sheets, gallery images, or video transcript; most execution claims are unverified.
No public repository is listed.
advance_reason: Potentially transformative WebMCP contribution and highly original protocol, despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: A shared floor-plan editor where humans manually edit and agents generate or optimize live layouts.
what_it_does: Lets users place rooms, doors, windows, furniture, and outdoor areas, while an agent reads the same state and creates variations from requirements.
leverage_rationale: High-level layout generation and continuation from human edits benefit substantially from structured shared state instead of many low-level canvas actions.
leverage_evidence: About text says UI and WebMCP tools use the same Zustand floor-plan state.
Agent can create layouts, optimize existing plans, and generate variations.
Frames and packaging show a floor-plan/design workspace with a large plan area and supporting panel.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the packet shows repeated planning/editor states, but the very low-contrast frame sheets do not establish the complete agent loop.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and a public repository is present.
Three frame sheets show wireframe/planning views and editor states.
Specific 1,800 sq ft requirements example is described.
impact_rationale: Home planners, designers, and space-planning users have a real iterative layout problem; agent variations can shorten exploration while preserving human control.
impact_evidence: Concrete requirements include bedrooms, maid room, storage, laundry, kitchen, garden, and parking.
Users can manually edit generated results and request further variations.
creativity_rationale: The human-and-agent co-editing model is a fresh, memorable use of WebMCP for a highly visual task.
creativity_evidence: Agent produces another plan below the human-created one rather than replacing the working plan.
The stated workflow explicitly continues from human edits.
usability_note: Visual editor metaphor is accessible, though the submitted frame sheets are low contrast and appear early-stage.
red_flags: Frame sheets are pale and low fidelity; exact states are difficult to verify.
No transcript demonstrates the request-to-layout flow.
standouts: Good fit between structured agent actions and visual human editing.
advance_reason: Distinctive collaborative interaction with meaningful WebMCP leverage and adequate product evidence.

one_line: Human-approved production incident recovery with temporary execution authority.
what_it_does: Agents inspect a simulated checkout incident, compare releases and logs, prepare an exact rollback, then execute only the approved plan and verify recovery.
leverage_rationale: Dynamic registration of execution authority after exact human approval is a meaningful capability change beyond browser clicking, especially for production-risk actions.
leverage_evidence: Six investigation/planning tools and a temporary execute_approved_recovery tool are specified.
Execution tool disappears after execution, rejection, revocation, reset, or expiry.
Frames show dark operational/audit screens and presenter/demo states; packaging shows approval emphasis.
execution_rationale: The incident narrative, tool set, approval boundary, and expected postconditions form a coherent complete scope, though the packet lacks transcript-level proof.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive and public repository present.
Specific release_284 mismatch and rollback to release_283 are described.
Claims include post-execution error rate, latency, DB status, and audit timeline changes.
impact_rationale: Production recovery is a high-value, high-risk workflow where faster diagnosis plus explicit approval and verification can directly reduce outage harm.
impact_evidence: Concrete checkout incident with 18.7% error rate and 1,420 ms P95 latency.
Human retains execution authority while agent handles investigation.
Verification and audit timeline are included.
creativity_rationale: The disappearing mutation capability and approval-bound recovery plan are an original, well-pursued interaction model for agentic operations.
creativity_evidence: Tool availability changes with authority state.
Plan fingerprint, expiry, risk, and exact approval are surfaced before mutation.
usability_note: The approval and audit framing appears clear; operational details may be dense for non-engineers.
red_flags: Simulated incident; no transcript and no direct observed execution.
Presenter-heavy frames reduce direct product-state evidence.
advance_reason: Very strong leverage and impact with a coherent, safety-conscious production workflow.

one_line: An agent-assisted lost-and-found catalog that turns fuzzy memories into evidence-based investigations.
what_it_does: Agents search and facet a catalog, inspect details, compare candidates, gather match evidence, pursue clues, and request a human claim decision.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, comparison, evidence, and resumable case tools improve reliability over UI driving, but a capable general agent could reproduce much of the outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Seven purpose-built investigation tools are listed.
Frames show light catalog/list/detail interfaces with item cards and browsing states.
Workflow supports imperfect-memory clues and human final decision.
execution_rationale: The catalog and investigation concept is coherent and visually supported by multiple browsing/detail states, though agent invocation is not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive and public repository present.
Three frame sheets show catalog, item-card, and detail-like states.
Specific tool sequence from search through claim request is described.
impact_rationale: Lost-property recovery is a concrete problem for communities and organizations, and clue-based narrowing fits how people actually remember items.
impact_evidence: Packet gives realistic fragmentary-memory examples such as a key ring and bear charm.
Agent narrows candidates while humans make the final claim decision.
creativity_rationale: It uses WebMCP for collaborative reasoning from imperfect clues rather than merely automating catalog buttons, giving the category a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Investigation can resume and request follow-up clues.
Explicit evidence comparison and human decision boundary.
usability_note: Catalog browsing and evidence cards appear approachable; the investigation model may need onboarding.
red_flags: No transcript; tool use is described rather than visibly confirmed.
Claim/matching quality is not independently evidenced.
standouts: Excellent fit for fuzzy human memory and agent evidence gathering.
advance_reason: Memorable concept with credible audience value and a real, if not transformative, structured-agent delta.

one_line: Compass packages selected personal context and permissions for a live, auditable agent workspace.
what_it_does: Stores local notes, tasks, bookmarks, and snippets; users create context packs with item and read/write constraints that govern agent tools.
leverage_rationale: The agent receives a user-controlled, live context boundary and tool registry that changes with permissions, which is materially safer and more precise than broad workspace UI access.
leverage_evidence: About text describes ten typed tools, active context reads, CRUD, task completion, linking, and pack creation.
Permission changes rebuild the registry immediately and handlers repeat checks.
Frames show Compass-branded dark dashboard/context panels and packaging identifies a personal-context product.
execution_rationale: Local-first data, validation, audit, undo, and a scripted Atlas flow indicate intentional completeness, but no transcript proves the complete sequence.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive and public repository present.
Uses IndexedDB/Dexie, Zod schemas, shared permission modules, and Vitest per the packet.
Included flow covers search, agent write, disable writes, disappearing surface, and undo.
impact_rationale: People using personal agents need useful context without granting unrestricted workspace access; this directly addresses privacy and control concerns.
impact_evidence: Context packs constrain spaces, item types, and read/write switches.
Agent writes appear in UI with readable audit entries and Undo.
Fictional Project Atlas gives an immediate task-management scenario.
creativity_rationale: Making the context boundary a temporary, understandable, permissioned object is a strong and original interaction model for personal agents.
creativity_evidence: Active Pack and dynamic write surface are central product concepts.
Local-first persistence plus live audit/undo is pursued coherently.
usability_note: Explicit packs, switches, audit entries, and Undo support user comprehension and recovery.
red_flags: No transcript or direct runtime observation.
Agent value depends on external WebMCP availability.
standouts: Concrete dynamic permission and undo workflow.
advance_reason: Well-evidenced, high-value personal-agent control model with meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: A browser music maker where an agent helps turn a human melody into an editable song.
what_it_does: Captures or imports vocal/melodic takes, then lets an agent suggest chords, add bass/drums, arrange, mix, play, undo, and export a song.
leverage_rationale: The agent needs exact musical notes, bars, tracks, revision state, audio clock, and cancellable export operations; structured tools substantially change reliability versus visual UI driving.
leverage_evidence: 29 tools expose song state, notes, chords, takes, alternatives, performance prompts, arrangement, mix, playback, undo/redo, and export.
Packet explains page-owned microphone, song document, audio clock, and speakers shared with the agent.
Frame sheet shows music-making/product UI and the packaging screenshot visibly shows a performer/audio-oriented demo.
execution_rationale: The product scope is ambitious but internally coherent, with many stated editing paths and a real video submission; no transcript limits verification of completion.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive, 176 seconds, public repository present.
Eight-bar starting song, five track kinds, audio retention, and multiple import/record paths are specified.
Frames show repeated music UI states.
impact_rationale: Beginners with musical ideas have a real barrier translating them into arrangements; an explainable collaborator that preserves and auditions alternatives offers credible creative value.
impact_evidence: Target user is a beginner who can hum/sing but cannot yet build chords, bass, drums, and arrangement.
Human can hear changes, choose alternatives, and use undo as a normal creative operation.
creativity_rationale: The teacher-producer agent and human-owned melody-to-arrangement collaboration are novel, ambitious, and especially well matched to browser audio capabilities.
creativity_evidence: Human performance is retained as a song take rather than discarded generation input.
Agent offers auditionable alternatives and asks the person to perform named parts over bars.
Cancellable multi-format export and revision controls deepen the concept.
usability_note: Audition, explain, undo, and familiar track concepts support beginners, though 29 tools imply significant complexity behind the scenes.
red_flags: Transcript is absent, so exact agent actions in the 176-second video are not confirmed.
Microphone/MIDI support may vary by browser.
standouts: WebMCP is tied to structured musical state rather than generic controls.
advance_reason: One of the packet's most original and WebMCP-native concepts, with real video and strong creative/impact value.

one_line: Captures a website’s design system and governs agent-generated pages against its rules.
what_it_does: Creates an interactive design wiki from a site, supplies rules to an AI, generates pages, and checks outputs for design-system violations.
leverage_rationale: Structured design-system extraction and rule checking give agents durable, precise constraints that visual browsing alone would struggle to preserve and enforce.
leverage_evidence: About text describes capture, design wiki, generation, strict governance, and telling the agent no when rules break.
Frames show public landing pages, dashboards, tables, and interactive wiki/playground states.
Packaging visibly presents BlockSmith as an AI website/design governance project.
execution_rationale: Multiple generated page types and an interactive wiki suggest a coherent pipeline, but no transcript or direct live validation establishes how automated checks behave.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive and public repository present.
Nine gallery images and three frame sheets show varied product surfaces.
Packet reports a Moda capture-to-wiki-to-custom-page flow and additional dashboard/chart outputs.
impact_rationale: Teams and designers have a real problem maintaining brand consistency while accelerating AI-generated web production; the proposed rule layer addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Targets recurring AI-generated brand failures such as wrong colors, spacing, and forbidden patterns.
Produces reusable design guidance and checks generated pages across landing, chart, and dashboard use cases.
creativity_rationale: Turning a rendered site into an interactive, enforceable design wiki is a fresh synthesis of reverse engineering, agent context, and governance.
creativity_evidence: Design wiki is interactive itself, including a component playground.
The product explicitly treats rules and rejection as part of the agent workflow, not just prompt text.
usability_note: A visual wiki/playground can make design rules legible; governance feedback quality is not directly demonstrated.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct evidence of rule violations being caught or rejected.
Some claims rely on self-reported generated examples.
standouts: Strong bridge between design systems and agent generation.
Interactive wiki makes otherwise implicit visual rules inspectable.
advance_reason: Clear audience problem, compelling design-governance concept, and meaningful structured-agent delta.

one_line: A professional network designed for humans and AI agents to discover, communicate, and collaborate.
what_it_does: Provides profiles, projects, feed, search, posts/comments, direct messages, and collaboration planning with WebMCP interaction paths.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, messaging, and collaboration tools can make agent participation more reliable, but general agents can achieve much of the same social-network outcome with UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text lists WebMCP flows for omni-search, DM sending, discovery, posting, and collaboration plans.
Nine gallery images show frontpage, profiles, DMs, posts/comments, and collaboration-plan surfaces.
No frame sheets were submitted.
execution_rationale: The packet shows broad feature ambition and extensive packaging imagery, but lacks frame sheets, video, public repo, and end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and nine gallery images are listed.
About text enumerates discovery and communication features.
Devpost packaging presents multiple named screens including DMs and collaboration plans.
impact_rationale: A professional network connecting human builders and agents has a plausible audience and useful discovery/collaboration goal, though network value is not demonstrated at scale.
impact_evidence: Target users are builders seeking distribution and collaboration.
Features cover project discovery, rich profiles, public activity, messaging, and plans.
creativity_rationale: Treating agents as first-class participants in a professional network is a fresh social interaction direction, even if the underlying feature set is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Explicit human-and-agent professional network framing.
WebMCP is used for agents to discover, communicate, post, and collaborate.
usability_note: Named screens suggest a recognizable social-network flow; breadth may create navigation complexity.
red_flags: No frame sheets, video, or public repository; execution and agent behavior are weakly evidenced.
Eligibility cannot be confidently established from the packet alone.
advance_reason: Interesting concept, but evidence is too thin and WebMCP delta is not clearly beyond conventional agent-enabled UI automation.

one_line: A real-time drawing-and-guessing game where humans and AI agents play together.
what_it_does: Players join synchronized rooms, take turns choosing prompts, drawing, guessing, chatting, and scoring, with ChatGPT participating through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Structured gameplay state and equal agent participation reduce the ambiguity of canvas, timers, turns, and private prompts, though a general agent could reproduce parts with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies eight imperative Website Tools for gameplay plus a REST fallback.
Shared Socket.IO state includes room, round, timer, score, chat, and canvas recovery.
No frame sheets were submitted; packaging shows a dark drawing-game presentation thumbnail.
execution_rationale: The described game loop and recovery behaviors are coherent and ambitious, but no video, frame sheets, or public repo provide direct execution evidence.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive.
Packet specifies real-time synchronization, room codes, mobile pointer support, reload recovery, and fallback behavior.
Devpost packaging presents a game/demo page but not an observed running session.
impact_rationale: The game offers credible entertainment and social value by making AI a participant rather than merely a generator.
impact_evidence: Clear audience of friends and AI agents in multiplayer drawing/guessing.
The human-AI interpretation and humor loop is the stated core desire.
Mobile-friendly and reload-recovery details support playability.
creativity_rationale: Making an AI an equal player in a shared Pictionary-like loop is memorable and more original than using AI only for generated content.
creativity_evidence: AI can draw, guess, chat, and participate in turns.
Private candidate words and human-agent interpretation are central to the design.
usability_note: Familiar drawing-game mechanics, room codes, and touch support are approachable; no live play evidence is available.
red_flags: No frame sheets, video, or public repo; core multiplayer and agent loop are not independently demonstrated.
REST fallback weakens the claim that WebMCP is essential.
standouts: AI is positioned as another player, not a content-generation button.
Good attention to multiplayer synchronization and reload recovery.
advance_reason: Highly creative game concept, but execution evidence and WebMCP indispensability are insufficient for advancement in this packet.
